channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Defesa de Flávio sobre Master vira pó em menos de 24 horas
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's defense regarding his financial ties to Daniel Vorcaro was deemed weak and disconnected from reality by critics. The allegations presented lack factual basis, as the facts are described as stubborn and undeniable. The defense's argument collapsed within 24 hours in the face of evidence.

item.title: Imprensa internacional repercute áudios de Flávio Bolsonaro para Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: International media outlets have amplified the leak of audio conversations between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro, revealing discussions about alleged political and financial negotiations. The recordings, published by Intercept Brasil, include references to potential influence over legislative decisions and conflicts of interest. The case has drawn global attention due to its ties to the Bolsonaro clan and raises concerns about transparency and corruption in Brazilian politics.

item.title: Flávio diz que ocultou relação com Vorcaro por contrato de confidencialidade
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) stated that he concealed his relationship with banker Daniel Vorcaro due to a confidentiality agreement. He said his only connection with Vorcaro was related to a specific matter, without elaborating. The statement was made in an interview with GloboNews on Thursday, November 14.

item.title: Entorno de Flávio aposta que áudio pode ter sido vazado para pressionar Mendonça por delação de Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s inner circle believes the leaked audio, in which he asks banker Daniel Vorcaro for money to fund Jair Bolsonaro’s biopic, was leaked to pressure Supreme Court Minister André Mendonça into quickly homologating Vorcaro’s plea deal. The leak allegedly came from individuals close to Vorcaro, aiming to threaten the Bolsonaro family with further damaging disclosures if the deal is not approved.

item.title: Mário Frias recua e diz haver 'diferença de interpretação sobre origem formal' de dinheiro que financiou filme sobre ex-presidente
item.description: Mário Frias walked back his earlier claim that the film 'Dark Horse' received no money from banker Daniel Vorcaro, clarifying that his initial statement referred only to the absence of a formal legal relationship, not actual funding. He acknowledged a 'difference in interpretation regarding the formal origin of the investment,' maintaining there is no material contradiction in his public positions. Audio released by Intercept Brasil shows Flávio Bolsonaro pressuring Vorcaro for overdue payments, confirming the existence of a financing contract for the film.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro alega que acordo de confidencialidade o impediu de revelar relação com Vorcaro: 'Não tem mais como negar'
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) stated that he omitted his relationship with banker Daniel Vorcaro due to a confidentiality clause tied to financing a film about former President Jair Bolsonaro, denying any wrongdoing and asserting the contact was purely commercial. He explained he only addressed the matter publicly now that it had become known, saying there was no longer a way to deny the connection.

item.title: "É um caso de polícia", diz Lula sobre relação entre Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Lula stated that the relationship between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro, arrested for financial fraud, is a 'police matter' and that he will not comment, as it is not his responsibility. The remark was made during a visit to a fertilizer plant in Bahia, in response to a journalist's question. The Intercept revealed that Flávio arranged R$ 134 million in transfers from Vorcaro to fund a film about Jair Bolsonaro, with payments occurring between February and May 2025.

item.title: ‘BolsoMaster’: vazamento de áudio de Flávio provoca a maior repercussão digital do caso Vorcaro
item.description: The leaked audio revealed that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro negotiated with banker Daniel Vorcaro a 134 million reais financing for a film about Jair Bolsonaro, triggering over 8.6 million social media interactions and establishing 'BolsoMaster' as the central axis of wear in his presidential pre-campaign. The Intercept Brasil report intensified suspicions of ties between Bolsonarismo and Banco Master, with Lula’s allies leveraging the case to undermine the senator’s pre-campaign.

item.title: Grilagem em xeque
item.description: The STF began reviewing the constitutionality of São Paulo State Law 17.557/2022, which allows the sale of public lands at drastically discounted prices—up to 90% below market value. Relator Minister Cármen Lúcia voted to annul the law, but Minister Gilmar Mendes requested a view, pausing the judgment for 90 days. The ADI, filed by the PT in 2022, criticizes the lack of technical studies, transparency, and beneficiary identification, alleging the policy favors land grabbers.

item.title: Lula joga sozinho
item.description: The article analyzes how former President Lula has been acting in political isolation ahead of the 2026 elections, lacking clear alliances or consistent support from traditional leaderships. Paulo Nogueira Batista Jr., economist and former vice-president of the BRICS New Development Bank, critiques this solitary political strategy, suggesting it may weaken governability and the coalition-building capacity needed to address national challenges.

item.title: O Nordeste é Lula
item.description: Senator Camilo Santana, coordinator of Lula’s campaign and former Education Minister, confirms that Elmano de Freitas remains the PT’s candidate for governor of Ceará, despite polls showing a tie with Ciro Gomes. He highlights the state’s advances in security, health, and education, including reduced homicides, expanded public health system, and record numbers of public school students admitted to universities. Santana notes that 75% of Ceará’s electorate remains undecided in spontaneous polling and that the campaign will contrast the government’s project with Gomes’ bolsonarism.

item.title: CARTUM: 1413
item.description: The article warns of democratic risks ahead of Brazil's 2026 elections, noting that while the Bolsonarist threat has retreated, it has not been defeated, with conservative forces still controlling Congress and global instability worsening. It urges readers to support critical, independent journalism by subscribing to or donating to CartaCapital.

item.title: Tragédia/ Explosão no Jaguaré
item.description: A Sabesp privatized sanitation company caused a gas leak in a Comgás pipeline that led to an explosion in Jaguaré, West Zone of São Paulo, destroying 46 homes, killing one resident and injuring three. The companies initially offered R$2,000 in emergency aid, later increased to R$5,000 under pressure, deemed insufficient by affected residents. The incident is cited as evidence of declining quality in privatized public services, comparable to recurring failures by Enel in the metropolitan area.

item.title: Na ponta do lápis
item.description: With less than a month to go before the 2026 World Cup, national teams are releasing preliminary squad lists, causing anxiety among fans. Injuries to players such as Estêvão (Brazil), Arrascaeta (Uruguay) and Mbappé (France) raise doubts about their participation, while the possible call-up of Neymar for Brazil remains the most debated topic in sports media. The author argues that Neymar, in good form and consistent with Santos, has the conditions to play in the World Cup and deserves peace to perform on the field.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes rejeita ação do PV que questionava sigilo de 100 anos no governo Tarcísio
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes rejected ADPF 1147 filed by the Green Party (PV), which challenged São Paulo State Decree 68.155/2023 regulating the Access to Information Law. Mendes ruled the decree merely reproduces federal law and that the ADPF is an inappropriate legal instrument for the matter, denying admission of the claim.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz que dinheiro pedido a Vorcaro foi 'integralmente para filme' e nega repasses a irmão Eduardo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro denies that funds obtained from Banco Master were used to cover expenses for his brother Eduardo Bolsonaro in the United States, stating that all money was fully allocated to the production of the film 'Dark Horse', a tribute to former President Jair Bolsonaro. He explains that his role was to seek private investors and that any payments to lawyers would relate to the management of the project's investment fund.

item.title: Entenda por que bolsa e dólar se recuperam após escândalo envolvendo Flávio e Vorcaro
item.description: Brazil's stock market and the dollar are recovering after volatility triggered by revelations that Flávio Bolsonaro sought funding for a film about his father, raising market concerns. The rebound is driven by stabilizing exchange rates due to constructive signals in U.S.-China trade talks, alongside anticipation of new polling to assess the political fallout. Despite Banco do Brasil's adjusted profit falling 53.5% in Q1 2026, its shares closed flat, reflecting investor caution.

item.title: A cena vazada de filme sobre Bolsonaro que teria recebido milhões de Vorcaro
item.description: A leaked scene from the film 'Dark Horse', depicting Jair Bolsonaro being stabbed in 2018, resurfaced following the release of audio exchanges between Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro, who allegedly invested R$ 61 million in the production. Starring Jim Caviezel, the film shows the actor seated on the shoulders of extras during the stabbing scene, drawing criticism for an unconvincing and caricatured performance, which became a target of online mockery. The movie, slated for release in 2026, had a clip from filming go viral in December 2025, causing embarrassment among Bolsonaro's right-wing supporters.

item.title: Mesmo diante de revelações, Bolsonaro sinaliza manutenção da pré-candidatura de Flávio
item.description: Despite revelations that Flávio Bolsonaro solicited payment from Daniel Vorcaro to complete a film about Jair Bolsonaro, the former president signaled he will maintain his son’s presidential pre-candidacy. PL allies expressed concern over Flávio’s political fragility, feeling betrayed for not being informed earlier of the risk, and acknowledge the candidacy will be tested in polls to measure the scandal’s impact. The substitution of the candidacy is not under consideration, not even by Michelle Bolsonaro, and right-wing rivals, such as Romeu Zema, are expected to exploit the vulnerability.

item.title: Após áudio de Flávio para Vorcaro, Frias nega que o Master seja investidor em biografia de Bolsonaro
item.description: Deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) denied that Banco Master is a formal investor in the Bolsonaro biopic 'Dark Horse', despite leaked audio showing Flávio Bolsonaro requesting funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro to continue filming. Frias clarified that while Vorcaro made requests for disbursements, neither he nor Banco Master are signatories to any legal contract with the film, and the formal investment was channeled through the distinct legal entity 'Entre'.

item.title: Lula ataca privatizações e legado de Bolsonaro
item.description: President Lula criticized privatizations and the economic legacy of previous governments during the resumption of operations at Petrobras' fertilizer factory in Bahia. Without directly naming Jair Bolsonaro, he attributed past administrations responsibility for decisions that harmed state-owned enterprises and national sovereignty.

item.title: De Ciro Nogueira a Vorcaro: sete golpes em sete dias que abalaram a direita nas eleições
item.description: Last week, Brazil's right-wing was shaken by a series of scandals, highlighted by a Federal Police operation against Ciro Nogueira, accused of receiving up to R$500,000 from former Banco Master owner Daniel Vorcaro to benefit the institution through unconstitutional amendments. Meanwhile, President Lula had a positive meeting with Donald Trump at the White House, where he was praised as 'very dynamic', contrasting with the previous week's setbacks for the government. These events, tied to the Master scandal and Lula's government performance, could significantly influence the 2026 elections despite political volatility.

item.title: Planalto não vê áudios como o fim de Flávio, e ataques ficam a cargo do PT
item.description: The Lula government views Flávio Bolsonaro's request for money from Daniel Vorcaro as damaging to the opposition, but not decisive for the 2026 election. Planalto officials believe the scandal is far from determining the outcome. However, the PT will take responsibility for keeping the issue alive to prevent it from being forgotten.

item.title: AP Exata: Áudio com Vorcaro derruba confiança em Flávio Bolsonaro nas redes e impulsiona Zema
item.description: A leaked audio containing messages from Flávio Bolsonaro to Daniel Vorcaro has undermined voter confidence in his presidential pre-campaign, sparking negative reactions on social media. The incident may damage his image and boost Zema’s candidacy, which benefits from the opponent’s weakening position.

item.title: TSE amplia acervo digital com decisões que moldaram a democracia
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has expanded its digital archive by updating the 'Historic Rulings' section, which functions as a digital museum of Brazilian democracy. The project, coordinated by the SGIC, organizes and contextualizes landmark electoral court decisions from recent decades, covering issues such as candidate eligibility and vote protection, with a focus on civic education and transparency. The initiative aims to allow citizens, students, and historians to explore jurisprudential milestones that have shaped the country's electoral system.

item.title: PT já postou 172 vezes nas redes sobre áudio de Flávio Bolsonaro a Vorcaro
item.description: The PT posted 172 times on social media in 24 hours regarding the leaked audio of Flávio Bolsonaro and Daniel Vorcaro, accounting for half of all political party posts and 73% of left-wing content. The scandal generated over 665,000 mentions, more than double the citations involving Lula, Ciro Nogueira, and the STF, with the progressive camp dominating engagement, especially on Instagram (2.5 million interactions). The right had broader reach only on YouTube, but the conservative camp totaled 2.6 million interactions across platforms, still behind the left.

item.title: Aliado de Flávio Bolsonaro aciona STF e TSE após reportagem do ‘Intercept’
item.description: Deputy Hélio Lopes (PL-RJ) filed a petition with the STF and TSE after The Intercept Brasil reported conversations between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and former Banco Master CEO Daniel Vorcaro regarding up to R$134 million in funding for the film Dark Horse, a biopic of Jair Bolsonaro. Lopes alleges selective leaks of confidential information and requests a criminal investigation, while The Intercept argues the move is an attempt to silence journalism and intimidate sources.

item.title: STF apura emenda parlamentar para produtora de filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino has ordered federal deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) to explain the allocation of R$2 million in parliamentary amendments to the National Academy of Culture (ANC), linked to the producer of the Bolsonaro biopic 'Dark Horse'. The probe suggests potential misuse of public funds to finance ideologically driven cinema, also involving deputies Tabata Amaral, Bia Kicis, and Marcos Pollon. A federal justice officer attempted to serve Frias three times between March and April without success, as his staff claimed he was in São Paulo on campaign duties.

item.title: Repasse a filme de Bolsonaro supera 3 vezes último filme de Caviezel
item.description: The R$ 61 million transferred by Daniel Vorcaro to the film "Dark Horse", about Jair Bolsonaro, is approximately three times the box office revenue of Jim Caviezel's last film, "International kidnapping". The financing was negotiated by Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for President, with intermediaries including Eduardo Bolsonaro and Mario Frias, and sent to a fund in the U.S. Flávio denies wrongdoing, stating it was private sponsorship without quid pro quo or public funds.

item.title: Flávio, Eduardo e produtores de filme sobre Bolsonaro divulgam informações conflitantes sobre financiamento do longa
item.description: Flávio and Eduardo Bolsonaro, along with allies and the producers of the film 'Dark Horse', have presented conflicting versions regarding the film's financing by Daniel Vorcaro's company, owner of Banco Master. Although Flávio initially denied the transfers, he later admitted seeking sponsorship, while the film's executive production claims no financing was received. The Federal Police are investigating whether the funds were used to support Eduardo's stay in the U.S., with documents showing R$ 61 million transferred out of a planned R$ 134 million.

item.title: Pimenta defende tornozeleira para Flávio por “risco de fuga”
item.description: Deputy Paulo Pimenta (PT-RS) stated that the governing coalition supports the use of an electronic ankle monitor on Senator Flávio Bolsonaro due to flight risk, citing his ties to former banker Daniel Vorcaro. The comment was made in a CNN Brasil interview and reflects concerns about potential attempts to evade justice.

item.title: Municípios e governo divergem sobre MP do piso dos professores
item.description: The CNM declared MP 1.334/2026 illegal and unconstitutional, stating it lacks a funding source and consumes 30% of municipal payroll. The government argues the measure ensures fiscal predictability and teacher valorization through a new formula combining last year's INPC with 50% of Fundeb's real revenue growth, raising the national teacher minimum wage from R$ 4.867,77 to R$ 5.130,63 in January 2026.

item.title: 'Caso dele é de polícia', diz Lula sobre conversas entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: Lula described the conversations between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro and banker Daniel Vorcaro regarding the financing of a film about Jair Bolsonaro as a 'police matter', stating it is not his responsibility to intervene. Vorcaro, imprisoned for allegedly leading a multibillion-dollar financial fraud scheme, reportedly paid R$ 61 million for the film 'Dark Horse', with funds transferred to a U.S.-based fund linked to Eduardo Bolsonaro. Lula emphasized his focus remains on governing for the Brazilian people, Petrobras, and employment.

item.title: Deputado do PT pede que PF siga dinheiro de Vorcaro até família Bolsonaro
item.description: Deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) filed a formal complaint with the Federal Police requesting an investigation into alleged use of Banco Master founder Daniel Vorcaro’s funds to finance an international political support structure for the Bolsonaro family in the U.S. The complaint highlights a $2 million transfer to Havengate Development Fund LP in Texas in February 2025 — coinciding with Eduardo Bolsonaro’s move to the U.S. — and cites evidence of money laundering, organized crime, and acts against national sovereignty.

item.title: Tabata reforça pedido de auditoria em emendas ligadas a filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: Deputy Tabata Amaral (PSB-SP) filed a supplementary brief at the STF regarding parliamentary amendment disbursements, alleging that Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, contributed R$62 million to a film about Jair Bolsonaro. The request seeks an audit of funds linked to the movie’s production.

item.title: ‘A verdade tarda, mas não falha’, diz Lula, um dia após revelações contra Flávio
item.description: President Lula stated that 'the truth is late, but it does not fail' during a visit to Minha Casa Minha Vida works in Camaçari, one day after revelations that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro asked banker Daniel Vorcaro for money to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro. The PT linked the comment to the allegations against Flávio, calling it the 'Bolsomaster scandal'.

item.title: STF tenta intimar Frias por emenda a ONG ligada a filme sobre Bolsonaro
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) has been attempting for over a month to summon federal deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) to provide information about possible irregularities in the execution of funds from parliamentary amendments directed to the Instituto Conhecer Brasil, an NGO linked to the producer of the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays the trajectory of former President Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Flávio é aconselhado pelo pai a “seguir firme” após vazamento de áudios
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro ruled out withdrawing from the presidential race following the leak of audio in which he spoke with banker Daniel Vorcaro, which also indicated the receipt of R$61 million. He said he was advised by his father, Jair Bolsonaro, to 'stay firm' amid the controversy. The material was published by The Intercept.

item.title: PT usa versículo bíblico e satiriza áudio de Flávio a Vorcaro
item.description: The PT published social media videos criticizing audio attributed to Flávio Bolsonaro, in which he allegedly requested money from Daniel Vorcaro to fund the film 'Dark Horse'. The party used the biblical verse Luke 8:17 — 'Nothing is hidden that will not be made known' — in a montage showing Flávio listening to the leaked audio, indirectly referencing Jair Bolsonaro’s frequent use of scripture. Despite internal guidance to avoid exaggeration, the PT intensified its response with at least 8 posts in 24 hours, focusing on the alleged transfer of US$10.6 million between February and May 2025.

item.title: Dark Horse não tem pedido de registro para lançamento no Brasil
item.description: GOUP Entertainment has not filed for commercial release of the film 'Dark Horse' in Brazil, despite Flávio Bolsonaro's claims of funding from Daniel Vorcaro. Mário Frias and the producer deny any financial contribution from Vorcaro, while Intercept Brasil and TV Globo confirmed R$61 million in payments for U.S. production between February and May 2025.

item.title: FLÁVIO CONTINUA NA FRENTE E LULA TEM MAIOR DESAPROVAÇÃO DE 52%
item.description: Flávio Dino remains ahead in the 2026 election polls, while President Lula records a 52% disapproval rating — the highest of his current term. Growing rejection of the federal government, particularly over economic and security issues, is benefiting the opposition.

item.title: A ‘contradição’ que está emperrando a eleição no Rio
item.description: The TSE has not yet ruled on appeals of Claudio Castro's conviction for abuse of political and economic power, leaving uncertainty over whether his resignation triggers a direct or indirect gubernatorial election in Rio. The STF awaits the TSE's decision on whether Castro lost his political rights, which determines the succession format. The delay favors the indirect vote scenario preferred by Castro's PL party, which controls the Alerj legislature, while the logistical window for a direct election closes on June 21.

item.title: Prêmio Innovare bate recorde de inscrições
item.description: The Innovare Award broke its registration record in the 23rd edition, with 807 initiatives submitted from across Brazil, surpassing the 774 from 2023. Registrations closed on May 5, and this year's theme is 'Responsible Public Administration: Transparency and Accountability to Society'. The award is organized by the Innovare Institute with support from judicial system institutions and Grupo Globo.

item.title: Deputados de esquerda pedem prisão preventiva de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Left-wing deputies from PCdoB, PT and Psol filed a criminal complaint with the PGR, requesting an investigation and preventive detention of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), a pre-candidate for president, over alleged financial and personal ties to Daniel Vorcaro, former controller of Banco Master, prior to his arrest. The request includes search and seizure, breaking banking and phone secrecy, and proposing a parliamentary inquiry (CPI) into Banco Master’s links with Bolsonarists. The Lula government base supports the move.

item.title: Jamais vou endossar proximidade de um candidato com um criminoso, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, former governor of Minas Gerais and pre-candidate for president, stated he would never accept as normal the proximity of Flávio Bolsonaro with a criminal, rejecting any endorsement of such associations.

item.title: Reação de Flávio a áudio irrita aliados, que temem mais estrago com Eduardo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign was caught off guard by the revelation that he asked Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Banco Master, for money to finance a film about his father, Jair Bolsonaro. Allies are trying to understand why he did not disclose the conversation found on the banker's phone, seized by the Federal Police last year, fearing it could cause further damage, especially involving Eduardo Bolsonaro.

item.title: Entenda a 'caixa-preta' do filme de Bolsonaro e por que orçamento é difícil de ser analisado
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro admitted requesting R$134 million from banker Daniel Vorcaro for the film Dark Horse, a tribute to his father Jair Bolsonaro, but claims he received only R$61 million. The production company Go Up Entertainment and screenwriter Mario Frias state they had no access to the funds, citing confidentiality agreements. Experts deem the budget excessive, given the modest recent careers of the involved artists, such as Jim Caviezel, whose notable work dates back over a decade.

item.title: STF ainda busca Mário Frias para esclarecer emenda para ONG ligada à produtora do filme de Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Flávio Dino has been attempting for over a month to summon Deputy Mário Frias (PL-SP) to clarify alleged irregularities in the allocation of R$ 2 million in parliamentary amendments to an NGO linked to the producer of the film Dark Horse, about Jair Bolsonaro. Frias has not been located at his offices in Brasília or São Paulo despite three attempts by a court officer. He denies receiving funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro for the film, contradicting statements by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: “Se tivesse sabido governar, o Lula não teria voltado nunca”, diz Caiado
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) stated that if the Bolsonaro government had governed well, President Lula would not have returned to power. He linked this to the amnesty decree on Lula’s first day in office, suggesting it was a reaction to prior mismanagement.

item.title: “Há um clima para suspender as alianças com o Novo em todos os estados”
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) publicly criticized Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) after messages exchanged with banker Daniel Vorcaro were revealed, sparking tension between the parties. Federal Deputy Júlia Zanatta (PL-SC) stated there is a growing sentiment within the PL to suspend any alliances with Novo across all states, due to dissatisfaction with Zema's conduct. The incident highlights a growing rift between the two right-wing parties, previously aligned on liberal agendas.
